raw_meta_yaml:
context:
  version: 0.13.0

package:
  name: polars-nanook
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  url: https://pypi.org/packages/source/p/polars-nanook/polars_nanook-${{ version }}.tar.gz
  sha256: 45b3a4ee8d273728b69cc9317dc2f280362f78063e3c8b037770422f9b475f1d

build:
  number: 0
  python:
    version_independent: true
    entry_points:
      - nanook=polars_nanook:cli_main
  skip:
    - not (match(python, python_min ~ ".*") and is_abi3)
  script:
    env:
      CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_STRIP: symbols
      CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO: fat
      CARGO: cargo-auditable-wrapper${{ '' if unix else '.bat' }}
    content:
      - if: unix
        then:
          - cp ${RECIPE_DIR}/cargo-auditable-wrapper.sh ${BUILD_PREFIX}/bin/cargo-auditable-wrapper
        else:
          - copy %RECIPE_DIR%\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat %BUILD_PREFIX%\Library\bin\cargo-auditable-wrapper.bat
      # aws-lc-sys only assembles its GAS-syntax aarch64 .S sources with clang-cl. It falls
      # back to clang-cl on its own only when CC is unset, but the vs2022 activation sets
      # CC_aarch64_pc_windows_msvc=cl.exe, which drops the .S files and fails with LNK1181.
      - if: target_platform == "win-arm64"
        then:
          - set "AWS_LC_SYS_CC=clang-cl"
      - python -m pip install . -vv --no-deps --no-build-isolation
      - cd client
      - cargo-bundle-licenses --format yaml --output ../THIRD_PARTY.yml

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('rust') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - cargo-auditable
    - cargo-bundle-licenses
    - libprotobuf
    - if: target_platform == "win-arm64"
      then:
        # provides clang-cl, needed to assemble the aarch64 sources of aws-lc-sys
        - clang
    - if: build_platform != target_platform
      then:
        - python
        - cross-python_${{ target_platform }}
        - maturin >=1,<2
  host:
    - python
    - python-abi3
    - pip
    - maturin >=1,<2
    - libprotobuf
  run:
    - python
    - polars ==2.1.0
    - polars-runtime-64 ==2.1.0
    - cloudpickle
    - typing_extensions >=4.5

tests:
  - if: not win
    then:
      python:
        imports:
          - polars_nanook
        pip_check: true
        python_version:
          - ${{ python_min }}.*
          - "*"
  # polars_nanook resolves its config directory on import, which fails in the
  # Windows test environment unless NANOOK_CONFIG_DIR is set
  - if: win
    then:
      script:
        env:
          NANOOK_CONFIG_DIR: nanook_config
        content:
          - python -c "import polars_nanook"
          - python -m pip check
      requirements:
        run:
          - python ${{ python_min }}.*
          - pip
  - script:
      env:
        NANOOK_CONFIG_DIR: nanook_config
      content:
        - nanook --help
  - script:
      content:
        - if: win
          then: abi3audit %SP_DIR%\polars_nanook\polars_nanook.pyd -s -v --assume-minimum-abi3 ${{ python_min }}
          else: abi3audit $SP_DIR/polars_nanook/polars_nanook.abi3.so -s -v --assume-minimum-abi3 ${{ python_min }}
    requirements:
      run:
        - abi3audit

about:
  homepage: https://pola.rs/nanook
  summary: Run Polars Nanook queries, managed or on-premises
  description: |
    Polars Nanook is the compute platform for Polars. The queries you write and test on your
    laptop run in production exactly as they are, with no rewrite and no new API. When your data
    outgrows one machine, the distributed engine scales the same query across a full cluster.
  license: MIT
  license_file:
    - LICENSE
    - THIRD_PARTY.yml
  documentation: https://docs.nanook.pola.rs/
  repository: https://github.com/pola-rs/polars-cloud-client

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - pavelzw
